title: Speed Initiative (RSI) — All-hands announcement draft
content:
Purpose / context:
- Quick internal announcement + talking points for the upcoming all-hands (Mar week). Lean, actionable, and gives folks a sense of what changes to expect in the next 90 days.
- Audience: whole company, but with emphasis on Eng, Product, SRE and Developer Experience.

Core headline (one-liner):
- Today we’re launching the Redwood Speed Initiative (RSI): a company-wide program to reduce median generation latency by 30% and unit cost per inference by 20% over Q2 while keeping quality neutral.

Why this matters (short bullets for comms slide):
- Faster inference improves product UX and conversion for API customers (direct revenue uplift).
- Lower per-token cost makes Dedicated and Private deployments more competitive at enterprise scale.
- Operational headroom: lower latency = fewer timeouts and fewer support headaches.

High-level commitments (what we’ll say we’re doing):
- Target metrics: median latency down 30%, p95 down 20%, cost/1M-token down 20% (baseline = Feb 2026 avg).
- Duration & cadence: 90-day sprint with weekly progress call and public dashboard updates in Console + internal tracking doc.
- Scope: serving runtime optimizations, kernel selection improvements, smarter batching defaults, and targeted model quantization experiments.
- Risk posture: gradual rollouts with canaries and automatic fallback; quality gates will block any rollout that shows regressions on our eval suites.

Planned visible milestones (for slides / timeline):
- Week 0–2: measure, baseline, prioritize top 5 request patterns and customer routes.
- Week 3–6: runtime micro-optimizations (KV cache improvements, better kernel heuristics), first Canary.
- Week 7–10: batching & routing defaults, model quantization pilots on low-risk fleets.
- Week 11–12: rollouts to hosted fleets, publish performance dashboard and docs for customers.

Talking points for founders (short, to read aloud):
- "We want Redwood to be the fastest inference platform engineers choose because speed matters — for user experience and for economics."
- "This is not a one-team project. We need Eng, Product, SRE, and Customer Success to move in sync — and we’ll share weekly wins and blockers."
- "We will ship carefully: any rollback will happen automatically if we detect quality drift."

Internal FAQ (draft):
Q: Will this change the models customers see?
A: No model behavior changes will be accepted without passing our quality gates. We will prefer runtime and routing changes first. When model variants are used (quantized or pruned), they will run behind canaries and be opt-in for private/dedicated until proven safe.

Q: Will this affect our SLAs?
A: Our goal is to improve latency while preserving availability. Any rollout that negatively impacts SLA metrics will be rolled back.

Q: How will CS/Support be kept in the loop?
A: Weekly digest + #rsi-status Slack channel. We’ll tag customer-impacting canaries and provide pre-made blurbs for support teams.

Q: Who owns the program?
A: Program leads: Marcus Flynn (Eng - Serving Runtime), Eleni Park (SRE), product sponsor Samir Patel. Comms lead: Priyanka Rao.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- [ ] Confirm Feb 2026 baseline numbers with runtime-metrics (ask Marcus for full extract).
- [ ] Finalize dashboard widget copy + owner (Product Ops).
- [ ] Get buy-in from Dedicated Ops for reserved-capacity canaries (Eleni).
- [ ] Prepare customer-facing FAQ for Hosted API docs (Samir to draft).
- [ ] Schedule 30-min pre-all-hands dry run with founders + tech leads (target Mar 10).

Risk notes (for founders slide or Q&A prep):
- Quality regressions from quantization experiments — mitigated via small-scale pilots and automatic gating.
- Ops complexity increases during rollouts — mitigation: runbook and dedicated SRE on-call for RSI rollouts.
- Customer confusion about "speed" vs "accuracy" — mitigation: clear docs and communication; emphasize quality gates and opt-in pilots.

Suggested flow for the all-hands segment (~6 minutes):
1) Founder intro (30s) — why speed matters.
2) Product/Eng lead (90s) — what RSI is and the metrics we’re chasing.
3) Demo quick clip (30s) — before/after generation latency on a representative request.
4) Ops/SRE (60s) — rollout safety & how we’ll communicate.
5) Closing + Where to find more info (30s) — link to Confluence, Slack channel, weekly digest sign-up.

Slack post draft (short):
- TL;DR: launching the Redwood Speed Initiative (RSI) to cut median latency ~30% and unit costs ~20% in Q2. We’re running a 90-day program with weekly updates in #rsi-status and a public dashboard coming soon. Ask questions here or join Thu’s sync.

Tone checklist (for copy):
- Clear, engineer-friendly, modestly ambitious.
- Avoid hype words: use "improve", "reduce", "pilot", "canary".
- Highlight safety and quality.

Notes from recent sync (copy in case helpful):
- Marcus: quantization pilot looks promising on smaller models, but 8-bit paths need more kernel work.
- Eleni: we need better rollback observability hooks before large-scale canaries.
- Samir: customers asking about cost reductions — good opportunity to link RSI to roadmap for Dedicated pricing.

Post-announcement follow-ups (operational items):
- Weekly digest template (comms) + who submits (Eng lead).
- Short internal survey at week 6 to capture regression reports & developer sentiment.
- Customer comms plan: decide if we proactively announce to all Hosted API customers after stable wins (yes/no).

Draft ending line for the all-hands slide: "Speed is a lever — we’ll move carefully, measure everything, and share wins transparently. Join the RSI channel to stay in the loop."

——
Notes-to-self: keep this doc informal — we’ll copy relevant lines into the slide deck and the Slack post. Don’t finalize FAQs until baseline numbers are in.
